content:
incident-bot: Pager: high latency + partial failures on /v1/generate in us-west-2. Impact: ~20% requests 500 / 2xx tail latency > 2s. Paging maya.
Maya (oncall): on it. joining bridge now — starting with checks: node health, gpu memory, routing table.
Jordan (sre): I can take logs + traces. @Maya share bridge link; I’ll pull the pre-tokenization errors and KV cache metrics.
Maya (oncall): bridge: https://call.bridge/abc123. paging @Liam for runtime knobs.
Liam (eng-runtime): here. I’ve seen a similar spike last month when kernel selection fell back to generic path. Will check kernel mismatch and tensor core errors.
Ravi (support): fielding inbound support chatter. I’ve flagged the top 3 customer tenants seeing errors: acme-inc, betaworks, example-saas.
Anya (product): ok — can we confirm customer-visible symptoms? Are they 500s or degraded quality?
Ravi (support): primarily 500s and timeouts, some streaming disconnects. Customers report "failed to generate".
Olivia (comms): drafting status page note. Need confirmed impact window and list of affected regions/tenants. Will assemble from this thread.
Jordan (sre): logs attached below (snip):
```
2026-06-12T14:02:11Z runtime[gpu-14]: kvcache miss ratio spike=0.78
2026-06-12T14:02:13Z runtime[worker-7]: kernel-fallback path taken: volatile
2026-06-12T14:02:15Z runtime[worker-7]: oom? alloc failed for 512MB tensor
```
Maya (oncall): hypothesis A: a recent canary pushed a quantized kernel that misbehaves at high batch sizes. Hypothesis B: autoscaler failed to spin up nodes so some hosts overloaded.
Liam (eng-runtime): checking canary history: we rolled kernel v2.4.3 to 10% at 13:55 UTC. Rollout policy shows "auto-bump" to 30% at 13:58 but failed midway. Investigating rollout logs.
Jordan (sre): meanwhile I'm assembling timeline. First error spike at 13:59:02 UTC, error volume climbs until 14:05, then intermittent recovery, then another spike at 14:18.
Maya (oncall): doing quick mitigation: lowering max-batch-size and disabling the new kernel via flag on the suspect pool. Liam — can you push a targeted fallback on pool-west-1?
Liam (eng-runtime): pushing config now: `runtime.pool.pool-west-1.kernel_override=stable-2.3.9` -> applied to 6/8 hosts. Rolling through. I'll post completion.
Liam (eng-runtime): done on 6 hosts, patching remaining 2 now.
Jordan (sre): I'm tailing logs; seeing error rate drop ~40% on patched hosts. Need full completion to verify.
Ravi (support): customers on patched hosts report improved behavior. acme-inc says they see fewer 500s.
Olivia (comms): tentative statuspage: "We experienced elevated error rates and increased latency for text generation in us-west-2 between ~13:59 and ongoing mitigation. We’ve applied a targeted rollback to a runtime kernel for affected hosts; customers may see gradual recovery. We’re investigating root cause and will update in 30 minutes." OK to post when we confirm drop?
Anya (product): add note: affected API route `/v1/generate` and streaming endpoints. Mention three known tenants.
Maya (oncall): timeline draft so far:
- 13:55 UTC: kernel v2.4.3 rollout started (10%)
- 13:58 UTC: rollout attempted increase -> partial failure
- 13:59 UTC: first error spike observed (500s, latency)
- 14:02 UTC: paging and bridge established
- 14:08 UTC: targeted kernel override started on pool-west-1
- 14:14 UTC: 75% hosts patched, errors dropping
- 14:20 UTC: mitigation applied cluster-wide, monitoring
Need someone to lock down the ambiguous events between 13:58-13:59 (what triggered the first spike).
Jordan (sre): I'll correlate deploy controller and autoscaler logs for 13:56-14:02. Sending extracts.
Jordan (sre): deploy controller shows `error: rollout step failed due to healthcheck flaps` at 13:58:43.
Liam (eng-runtime): autoscaler metrics show a short window where new hosts didn't join due to cloud API throttling from refresh token rotation at 13:57:58 — that may have made the initial 10% more impactful.
Maya (oncall): ok so combined theory: incomplete rollout + throttled autoscaler -> capacity gap -> kernel fallback + OOMs under high load.
Ravi (support): customers want ETA for full recovery. What should I tell them?
Maya (oncall): tell them "we are seeing gradual recovery after a targeted rollback; expect >90% recovery in 10-15 minutes, full verification in 60 minutes." Add that support will follow up with tenant-specific notes.
Olivia (comms): preparing statuspage now. Draft:
"At ~13:59 UTC we observed increased errors and latency for the text-generation API in us-west-2. A recent runtime kernel rollout plus a temporary autoscaler capacity gap contributed. We applied a rollback to the previous kernel version and are monitoring system recovery. Affected customers: acme-inc, betaworks, example-saas. Impact window under investigation. Next update in 30 minutes."
Anya (product): please include contact escalation for enterprise customers; add "If you are enterprise and need immediate assistance, contact your AM."
Maya (oncall): action items:
- Jordan: correlate deploy, autoscaler, and kernel logs for 13:55-14:05 (timeline + evidence) — assigned
- Liam: verify rollback completed on all pools and document rollout flags changed — assigned
- Olivia: post status page once we confirm 50% error reduction — assigned
- Ravi: customer follow-ups (acme/betaworks/example) — assigned
- Maya: write initial RCA skeleton after logs are in (timeline, root cause, mitigations)
Jordan (sre): capturing logs now. Sharing pastebin: https://logs.redwood/paste/xyz789 (contains deploy/controller, autoscaler, runtime traces).
Liam (eng-runtime): completed kernel override on remaining hosts at 14:24 UTC. All hosts now stable on stable-2.3.9.
Jordan (sre): correlation notes:
```
13:56:20 deploy-controller: rollout-step(42) -> started
13:57:58 cloud-api: token-rotate throttle error
13:58:43 deploy-controller: rollout-step failed, paused
13:59:00 runtime: error spike begin
14:08:10 runtime: kernel_override applied to pool-west-1
14:14:30 error-rate: down 60%
14:24:00 full override applied
```
Maya (oncall): final checks: tail latency back to baseline on 95% hosts, error rate <1% on patched hosts. I think we can move to post-incident comms. Olivia — please post the status page with the timeline we have and note ongoing RCA.
Olivia (comms): published status update and pinned in channel. Link: https://status.redwood/incident/2026-06-12-1849001111
Ravi (support): sending customer-specific notes now.
Anya (product): will schedule a 1-hour RCA meeting tomorrow for deeper follow-up. Also we should discuss hardening the autoscaler token refresh path.
Maya (oncall): closing loop: final remediation suggestions — stop auto-bump rollouts for kernel changes, require node diversification and safety checks when autoscaler shows throttling, add alert for deploy-controller rollout fallback.
Jordan (sre): adding those to the RCA draft. Will attach logs and metric graphs.
Liam (eng-runtime): will add a failsafe to detect kernel fallback path usage > 5% and automatically demote new kernel.
Olivia (comms): thanks team. posting summary to stakeholders and tagging AMs.
Maya (oncall): thanks everyone — marking thread for post-incident writeup. If anything else pops up, reply here. :white_check_mark:
